headline: WorkOS, Northflank and Trigger.dev disclose AI-linked hacks; cPGuard supply chain attack and exploited WordPress flaw stay on top

bullets.text: New: SecurityWeek reports WorkOS, Northflank and Trigger.dev have disclosed hacks in a mounting run of AI-linked breaches. BleepingComputer says the WorkOS attacker used ARTEX AI to breach an internal sales app.
Still active, cPGuard, 4 outlets: Help Net Security says a poisoned update hit thousands of web hosting servers. BleepingComputer reports the hijacked autoupdate deployed a backdoor and stole data.

Still active, WordPress Core, 3 outlets: BleepingComputer reports CISA flags a WordPress RCE flaw as actively exploited. CISA KEV lists CVE-2026-119977, a race condition added 2026-11-03, with a federal due date of 2026-11-06.
Still active: The Hacker News reports a critical Rails flaw lets attackers write server files through crafted ImageMagick uploads.
Still active, $6.3B Binance heist, 8 outlets: SecurityWeek reports a rigged coding assignment and an abused AI tool opened the path to the theft.

Still active, Connect Secure, 4 outlets: Ivanti patched two more zero-days chained in attacks, CVE-2026-111357 and CVE-2026-118527. CISA KEV lists CVE-2026-104935 in the same product, with federal due dates of 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-13.

actions: If you use WorkOS, Northflank or Trigger.dev, read their disclosures and review the access and tokens you share with them.
If you run cPGuard, check servers for the backdoor reported by BleepingComputer and treat data on affected hosts as exposed.
Update WordPress Core for CVE-2026-119977 per vendor guidance; the KEV federal due date is 2026-11-06.
Find Rails apps that process ImageMagick uploads, follow the Rails project's guidance, and check for unexpected files on those servers.
Apply Ivanti's latest Connect Secure patches, covering CVE-2026-111357 and CVE-2026-118527, and check appliances for compromise.
Find Node-RED instances, patch CVE-2026-58115 per vendor guidance, and look for backdoors.
